paragraphs: Direct assessment: Layout work merits further exploration if you will interpret dimensions from engineering drawings, select datums, position workpieces and leave reviewable markings, while remaining responsible for positioning, hoisting and stabilizing metal and plastic workpieces.

Observable signals: Assess layout-work fit through dimensional tasks: maintaining datums, recording steps and finding contradictions; proactively confirming units and versions when reading drawings; determining datums and working surfaces before marking; and checking calculations by a second method. Caution conditions: pause and ask when unclear; explain exceptions and pending confirmations at handoff. Work may involve handling, positioning and proximity to large workpieces, as well as seated calculations.

Safe work sample (an entirely fictional layout-worker task package): Within 60 minutes, organize metal/plastic workpieces, engineering drawings and templates, and measuring/marking tools; interpret drawing dimensions, locate datums and mark layouts, review dimensional markings, and produce results, review points and escalation records. Inputs must contain no real personal, customer, patient or employer-confidential information.

Sample outputs and reflection: Check whether positioning, hoisting and stabilization of metal/plastic workpieces are addressed, with permissions and uncertainties clearly identified. Ask whether you can explain each judgment, identify errors and proactively escalate at boundaries.

Layout workers correspond to U.S. 51-4192.00: establishing reference points and dimensions for subsequent processing on metal or plastic stock, tubes, structural parts, castings or machine parts, including shipfitters. Duties include calculating layouts, marking curves, hole locations and welding symbols, checking centerlines and templates, aligning assemblies and positioning workpieces. Actual hoisting, welding and equipment operation each require employer training and authorization, not granted by an occupational title.

entries: Work objects: metal and plastic workpieces, engineering drawings and templates, measuring and marking tools, dimensions and tolerances, datums and processing sequences.
Inspectable outputs: dimensions calculated from drawings and established datums, with reviewable layout markings, inspection records and exception-escalation records.

Complete workflow: read drawings and verify versions and units, select datums and calculate dimensions, position and mark, review markings, plan cutting, drilling, bending or welding sequence, then hand off with records.

paragraphs: Key judgments | Verify dimensions and template positions against drawing revision, units, datums and tolerances; confirm working surfaces before marking. Review calculations and physical positioning separately; do not independently choose a version and release work when conflicts arise.

O*NET U.S. respondents: common protective equipment daily 100%; accuracy extremely important 69% / very important 31%; contaminants daily 87%, distracting noise daily 65%; time pressure daily 18%, weekly but not daily 37%, never 36%. These are not Chinese accident rates, uniform shifts or a PPE checklist for every job.

O*NET interest RC (R91/C48/A31/I31/E0/S0) reflects activity preferences, not ability. Task tools include scribers, marking stones, punches, dividers, protractors, gauge blocks, height gauges and dial indicators; CAD lists AutoCAD, but software listings are not proficiency. U.S. 2025 industries: manufacturing 63%, government 18%, administrative support 11%, with remaining 8% calculated as the difference. BLS51-4192 typically lists high school or equivalent, no related experience and moderate-term on-the-job training; do not extrapolate a uniform Chinese threshold.

Collaboration chain | Arrange layouts using upstream drawings and versions, handing markings, datums, dimensional rationale and exceptions to machining and assembly personnel. O*NET lists communication with supervisors and colleagues; verify specific quality-release and hoisting-command relationships at each factory.
Quality standards: controlled workpiece positioning, hoisting and stabilization; traceable datums and dimensions; reviewed markings; and authorized escalation of exceptions.

Boundaries with adjacent roles: This page covers only U.S. O*NET-SOC 51-4192.00, Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic. Tools or proxy definitions cannot replace adjacent-role boundaries, institutional authorization, licensing, sign-off authority or final responsibility.
Adjacent roles also handle metal or plastic, but layout workers' key output is transmitting datums and dimensions before processing.

Insufficient evidence: This round obtained no occupational generative AI adoption rate or measured efficiency gains. Organization can be trialed on fictional drawing records, with humans checking units, datums and versions; a CAD list does not demonstrate generative AI.

Evidence definition | BLS factors for three industries concern programmable processes/equipment and capital substitution, not generative AI causation. O*NET2025 hot technologies lists AutoCAD/Excel/Office/PPT/Word, all five Not available; do not enter 0. NIST's voluntary risk framework does not measure occupational effects.

Human control points | Verify drawing versions, materials, measuring tools, working surfaces, datums and markings; trained, authorized personnel are responsible for actual workpiece positioning, hoisting and quality release.

Responsibility chain | Retain drawing revisions, dimensional calculations, inspection and handoff records. Tools cannot approve dimensional release, authorize hoisting or replace equipment safety controls.
Action suggestion | Check units, datums and errors in paper records; handle actual workpieces and equipment under employer training and permissions, without promising efficiency gains.

Employment evidence | BLS2025—2035 exact projections show a decline of 3.4% and average annual openings of 500, including replacement. This cannot establish generative-AI-caused job cuts or individual hiring probability.
Trial scope | Only organize fictional drawing versions, dimensions and pending checks; do not automatically produce actual processing parameters or safety releases.

The Chinese term layout worker describes this page's tasks; U.S. 51-4192 includes shipfitters. The same Chinese name does not establish strict statistical equivalence in China. Exact nationwide Chinese occupational pay is unestablished in this round; do not turn that gap into a claim that public statistics contain no single-occupation data at all.

Chinese industry context | NBS2025 manufacturing urban non-private 113,594 and private 76,055 yuan/year are pretax annual averages. The industry includes many occupations and excludes individual businesses and freelancers. List the two types separately, not as a layout-worker pay range or starting pay. Verify pay calculation, shifts and duties with the target factory separately.

Insufficient evidence: This bounded search did not establish a nationwide mainland China occupational pay distribution exactly matching U.S. O*NET-SOC 51-4192.00 layout workers. Therefore no starting pay, median or percentiles are generated, and industry averages, recruitment offers or U.S. figures are not used to fill the gap.

This round established no causal relationship involving layout-worker AI adoption, efficiency gains or pay changes. Separate CAD and programmable equipment from generative AI; verify actual duties, training, pay periods and shifts when job seeking, without asserting AI cannot change pay factors.

Task signal: Assess layout-work fit through dimensional tasks—maintaining datums, recording steps and finding contradictions—because these directly affect positioning, hoisting and stabilization of metal/plastic workpieces.
Task signal: Proactively confirm units and versions when reading drawings, because these directly affect positioning, hoisting and stabilization of metal/plastic workpieces.
Task signal: Determine datums and working surfaces before marking, because these directly affect positioning, hoisting and stabilization of metal/plastic workpieces.
Task signal: Check calculations using a second method, because this directly affects positioning, hoisting and stabilization of metal/plastic workpieces.
Caution condition: Pause and ask when unclear; prioritize comparison with adjacent roles or different employer settings.
RC interests only guide observation of drawing reading, calculation, review and workpiece coordination; they predict neither ability nor authorization.

This round did not establish personality's predictive validity for layout-worker performance. Verify employer training and support for physical handling and positioning demands, using records and actual supervisory feedback.
RIASEC or personality frameworks only help formulate questions; they cannot replace layout-worker work samples, learning ability, qualifications or actual performance evidence.

Sharp edges and moving machinery | Trigger: handling sharp-edged workpieces or approaching pinch points and moving parts. Consequences: cuts, crushing or amputation. Controls: first verify workpiece stability, guarding and exclusion areas, and select protection under the employer's risk assessment. Untrained people must not enter moving-part danger zones.

Dimension and datum errors | Trigger: marking and releasing despite unit, revision or datum conflicts. Consequences: rework, scrap or downstream assembly mismatch. Controls: pause affected layout work, double-check original drawings and critical dimensions, and retain exceptions for the quality responsible person.

Hazardous energy | Trigger: entering a maintenance danger zone after only pressing stop. Consequences: unexpected startup or residual-energy injury. Controls: trained, authorized personnel perform applicable LOTO, isolate energy, control stored energy and verify. Stop buttons are not isolation; others must not remove locks or restart.

Workpiece positioning and hoisting | Trigger: unstable support or unverified weight, rigging and command relationships. Consequences: tipping, crushing or collision. Controls: pause movement and ask trained responsible personnel to verify support, weight and approved plans. O*NET handling duties do not grant hoisting qualifications.

Contaminants and noise | Trigger: unverified task exposures and protection requirements. Consequences: potential health and communication effects. Controls: employers assess specific exposure and provide training and protection; O*NET response frequencies are neither accident rates nor a basis for choosing respirators independently.
Practical entry: Typical U.S. entry is high school or equivalent, no related experience and moderate-term on-the-job training. First confirm first-year tasks and supervision.

Employer evidence: Specific factories have different training requirements for measuring tools, hoisting, nearby welding and equipment permissions; verify each role. Demonstrate reviewable capabilities rather than merely listing course names.

Work sample without experience: An entirely fictional layout-worker task package. Within 60 minutes, organize metal/plastic workpieces, engineering drawings and templates, and measuring/marking tools; interpret dimensions, locate datums and mark, review dimensional markings, and produce results, review points and escalation records, without real sensitive data.

Interviews and probation | Explain drawing versions, units, datums, critical-dimension checks and exception handoff. Actual workpiece positioning, hoisting and machinery operation require employer training and authorization; work samples grant no permissions.

Seven-day trial: Understand objects and workflows in the first two days, complete and review a sample in the middle three days, ask others to challenge it on day six, and write evidence for continuing/stopping/changing direction on day seven.

Qualification decisions: Practice only with cardboard, paper drawings and nonhazardous measuring tools; operate no real machine tools or sharp-edged metal. Certification, hiring, authorization and sign-off responsibility are different statuses.
Capability ladder: First learn mechanical drawing, dimensions and tolerances, basic trigonometry, measuring tools and workpiece datums. Advancement rests on reviewable work, not guaranteed years.

Transition pathway: Day 1 read drawings; day 2 practice measuring tools; day 3 calculate dimensions; day 4 set datums; day 5 mark cardboard; day 6 independently review; day 7 write a handoff. Before transitioning, list transferable capabilities and gaps in qualifications, tools and responsibility experience.

U.S. exact occupation 51-4192: employment 6,200 in 2025 → 5,900 in 2035; table-listed net change -200 people, -3.4%, average annual openings 500. Retain table-rounded endpoints and net change; do not recreate figures by subtraction.
Explain employment, growth rate, net change and annual openings separately; do not combine them into an individual employment guarantee.

BLS2025—2035 average annual openings of 500 include growth and replacement. Overall occupational employment is projected to decline; openings are neither net new jobs nor current hiring. Exact nationwide Chinese demand is unestablished.

BLS lists programmable-equipment substitution/productivity factors separately for fabricated metals, aerospace and shipbuilding; these are not measured generative AI adoption or occupational AI effects. Compare drawing reading, dimensions, templates and quality records for transfer.

Adjacent directions need specialized additions: milling/planing needs workholding, cutters and machine-tool training; model making needs shaping and assembly; nonmetal/plastic molding needs target-material processes; metal/plastic patternmaking needs pattern-manufacturing evidence. No automatic transfer or operating permissions are granted.

source_card.note: Verify O*NET51-4192 tasks / RC/2025 industries and exact BLS projections separately. This round verified median wage 63870/hourly 30.71; original 2025 endpoint percentiles were not reacquired, and 25/75 gaps remain unfilled. NBS manufacturing's two 2025 annual averages are industry context only. BLS industry factors concern programmable equipment; NIST is a risk framework; no measured occupational generative AI adoption exists here. OSHA3170 is 2007 technical guidance and 3120 energy-control material, neither current Chinese law nor occupational accident rates. Shared protected source-template notes retain the scope conflict; body text no longer displays their generic claims.

description.text: Layout workers turn layout work into calculations and datum establishment using measuring tools. Assess this career through the work loop, responsibility boundaries, evidence definitions, risk controls and observable entry-level work samples.

title.text: Layout Worker Career Assessment: Work, Entry and Risk Boundaries

subject.name: Layout Workers, Metal and Plastic
subject.summary: Layout workers interpret dimensions from engineering drawings and templates on metal or plastic workpieces, select datums, position workpieces and leave reviewable marks so downstream processing knows where to begin. Assess this career by checking the work loop, responsibility boundaries, evidence definitions, safety risks and observable entry-level work samples.
